design_detail: Retraction note, not a study (Psychopharmacology vol. 241, p. 2405, November 2024 issue; published online 10 August 2024; open access, CC BY), retracting the article by Mithoefer M. C., Feduccia, Jerome, Mithoefer A., Wagner, Walsh, Hamilton, Yazar-Klosinski, Emerson and Doblin that set out the study design and rationale for the phase 3 trials of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for PTSD from a pooled analysis of six phase 2 randomized controlled trials (Psychopharmacology 236:2735-2745; published online 7 May 2019; full title in Crossref). Two short paragraphs, no data. Read on the publisher's page (link.springer.com, reached through doi.org) in the app's browser; the Crossref records of the notice and of the retracted article were read in the same tab. Card design 'narrative-review' is the schema's closest category for an editorial notice. Reference id assigned by this reader (first author in Crossref plus year; distinct from mithoefer_2003); the reference record is to be built by the editor from the Crossref line added to the cache.
can_establish: That Psychopharmacology retracted, on 10 August 2024, the pooled analysis of six phase 2 trials that set out the design and rationale for the phase 3 trials, the grounds the editors gave, and which authors agreed, disagreed, abstained or did not respond.
cannot_establish: What the protocol violations at the MP4 site were, which of the six trials the site belonged to, how much of the pooled data came from it, whether the pooled results would change without them, or anything about the phase 3 trials themselves, which the notice does not mention.

analysis.selective_reporting: The notice does not describe the violations, does not say which authors confirmed knowing of them, and does not say which trial or how much of the pooled data the MP4 site contributed.

interpretation_gap.results_show: An editorial decision and its stated grounds: protocol violations amounting to unethical conduct at the MP4 study site, known to the authors at submission and neither disclosed to the journal nor removed from the analysis; and a potential competing interest not fully declared.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The notice claims nothing beyond its grounds and the authors' positions. It speaks of 'this trial', although the article, by its title, pooled six phase 2 trials, and it says nothing about the phase 3 trials whose design the article set out.

timeline.event: The article, setting out the design and rationale for the phase 3 trials from six pooled phase 2 trials, is published online (7 May 2019; print issue September 2019 per Crossref).
First phase 3 trial published (Mitchell et al., 2021).
Second phase 3 trial published (Mitchell et al., 2023).
This retraction note (10 August 2024), issued the same day as the notes for two other phase 2 analyses from the same programme (Feduccia et al., 2024; Jerome et al., 2024).
The BMJ reports the three retractions (Mahase, 2024).

replication.where_it_stands: Retracted. Under METHODS §4.3 the retracted article cannot support any claim; this notice may be cited for the fact of the retraction and its stated grounds. The phase 3 trial reports are separate publications and are not retracted by this notice.

funding.funder: Not applicable (notice). The notice states, from the article's funding declaration, that MAPS fully funded and provided the MDMA used and that MAPS PBC organised the trial.
funding.declared_conflicts: Per the notice, the authors did not fully declare a potential competing interest: several of the authors are affiliated with either MAPS or MAPS PBC, a subsidiary wholly owned by MAPS.
funding.affiliations_note: Affiliations listed with the notice: Michael C. Mithoefer and Mark Wagner, Medical University of South Carolina; Allison A. Feduccia, Lisa Jerome and Amy Emerson, MAPS Public Benefit Corporation, Santa Cruz, CA; Anne Mithoefer, private practice, Charleston, SC; Zach Walsh, University of British Columbia-Okanagan; Scott Hamilton, Stanford School of Medicine; Berra Yazar-Klosinski and Rick Doblin, Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies, Santa Cruz, CA.

what_would_settle_it: For the article's question: the pooled phase 2 analysis re-run without the MP4 site's data and published; for the phase 3 programme, the regulator's assessment of whether its design or data were affected.

domains.note: Not a review: the notice reports the editors' own decision on one article, so nothing is selected.
The notice does not say how the violations were established, which of the six trials the site belonged to, or how much of the pooled data came from it.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies

domains.note: States the decision and its grounds without speculation.

domains.domain: Balance of views on the retraction (the authors' positions)
domains.note: Records which authors agree, disagree, neither agree nor disagree, or did not respond.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to retraction notices; the editors' narrative-review checklist is used as the closest available, its domains read as questions about the notice as a source. The notice is the primary record of the retraction and its stated grounds and may be cited for both; it gives no account of the violations and no reanalysis, and it does not address the phase 3 trials.

key_findings.finding: Retraction note published 10 August 2024 (Psychopharmacology 241, p. 2405; issue date November 2024) for the original article published on 7 May 2019, cited in the notice as Psychopharmacology (2019) 236:2735-2745, doi 10.1007/s00213-019-05249-5.
key_findings.locator: Article header; 'The Original Article was published on' line

key_findings.finding: The editors retracted the article after they were informed of protocol violations amounting to unethical conduct at the MP4 study site by researchers associated with the project. The authors then confirmed that they had known of these violations when they submitted the article but did not disclose this to the journal or remove that site's data from their analysis.

The authors also did not fully declare a potential competing interest: several of the authors are affiliated with either MAPS or MAPS PBC, a subsidiary wholly owned by MAPS. As the article's funding declaration stated, MAPS fully funded and provided the MDMA used, and MAPS PBC organised the trial.

Allison A. Feduccia agrees with the retraction but disagrees with the wording of the notice; Michael C. Mithoefer, Lisa Jerome, Anne Mithoefer, Mark Wagner, Berra Yazar-Klosinski and Rick Doblin disagree; Zach Walsh neither agrees nor disagrees; the remaining authors did not respond to the publisher's correspondence (editors' reading of the author list: Scott Hamilton and Amy Emerson).
key_findings.locator: Retraction note text, 2nd paragraph; author list

key_findings.finding: The notice's Crossref record (vol. 241, issue 11, page 2405; online 10 August 2024, print November 2024; ten authors, M. C. Mithoefer first) carries an update-to link of type 'retraction', from both Retraction Watch and the publisher, dated 10 August 2024, pointing to 10.1007/s00213-019-05249-5; that article's record carries the matching updated-by link, its title now begins 'RETRACTED ARTICLE', and its print issue is given as September 2019 (vol. 236, issue 9, pp. 2735-2745).

reporting_issues.issue: The notice refers to 'this trial' and to data generated by the MP4 site, although the article, by its title, is a pooled analysis of six phase 2 trials; it does not say which of them included the MP4 site or how much of the pooled data came from it.
reporting_issues.consequence: The size of the problem in the pooled phase 2 data, and any bearing on the phase 3 design the article set out, cannot be judged from the notice.

reporting_issues.issue: The notice says 'the authors' confirmed knowing of the violations at submission, without saying which authors; six authors disagree with the retraction, one neither agrees nor disagrees, and two did not respond.
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the notice's wording; do not attribute the confirmation to any named author.

reporting_issues.issue: The notice says the editors were informed of protocol violations amounting to unethical conduct at the MP4 study site 'by researchers associated with this project', a phrase that can name either who informed the editors or whose conduct it was; the BMJ reads it as conduct by researchers. The notice gives no date for when the editors were informed or for the violations.
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the notice's own wording and do not resolve the ambiguity. For timing, the sponsor's own public statement of an ethical violation by former MAPS-sponsored investigators is dated 24 May 2019 by its URL (Mahase, 2024, reference 5; not read); whether it concerns MP4 is not stated in the sources read.
